18/G.goal: Explain the main tracking technologies used in VR and AR, how they estimate position and orientation, and how hybrid systems combine them.
18/G.achieves: It provides the foundational understanding of tracking needed to evaluate XR hardware and software choices and to design and implement an XR system confidently.

18/O1.goal: Explain the main categories of XR tracking and how electromechanical, electromagnetic, and acoustic/ultrasonic trackers estimate position and orientation.
18/O1.achieves: It gives the learner a first framework for distinguishing tracking hardware and software options in later XR system discussions.

18/O2.goal: Explain how vision-based and structure-based tracking methods use optical or depth sensing to estimate pose.
18/O2.achieves: It lets the learner understand camera- and depth-based tracking choices and their implications for accuracy, performance, and XR system design.

18/O3.goal: Describe how sensor-based and hybrid tracking methods use inertial, positional, motion-capture, and eye-tracking data, including their limitations.
18/O3.achieves: It enables the learner to recognize how XR interaction can track the whole body, gaze, or a combination of signals, and to identify limitations when selecting tracking approaches.
